scripts.//format: Prettier is adopted in report-only mode: the config is authoritative for new and touched files, but the ~86 pre-existing files have not been reflowed, so `format:check` is not part of `verify` yet. Run `yarn format` as its own commit to switch it on — do that alone, never mixed with a change, or the reflow buries the real diff.
scripts.//verify: What CI runs, and the one command to run before pushing.
scripts.verify: yarn lint && yarn typecheck && yarn build

comments.resolutions: babel-loader 8 resolves @babel/core from the hoisted root, but @babel/preset-react 7 asserts a peer of ^7.0.0-0 and throws on 8.x. Without this pin an install that hoists @babel/core 8 broke every babel-loader package with 'Requires Babel ^7.0.0-0, but was loaded with 8.x'. No webpack config uses babel-loader any longer — `home` dropped it with its JSX, `nav` became TypeScript custom elements and `icd10` became Vue — so the pin is now vestigial and kept only because `home` still *declares* @babel/core and @babel/preset-react. Remove it in the same change that drops those three dependencies, not before: the failure it prevents is an install-time peer assertion, so an install is the only thing that can prove it is safe to lift.
comments.lint-versions: The lint toolchain is pinned exactly, not ranged. typescript-eslint's `typescript` peer is an upper-bounded range (`>=4.8.4 <6.1.0`) and this repo is on TS 6, so a caret range would let an install pick a version that refuses to resolve. 8.65.0 is the lowest release whose peer range admits TS 6. `vue-eslint-parser` is pinned for the same reason and lives here rather than in the `icd10` workspace: `eslint.config.mjs` is at the root and imports it directly, so it has to resolve from the root regardless of which package the `.vue` files are in.
